title: Enterprise model intake: prioritization framework & per-customer gating process
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization framework for enterprise customer requests to add, pin, or deprecate models in the Redwood model catalog. Focus on non-bug requests coming from dedicated/private customers and sales/solutions engineering: new model additions, version pinning for regulatory reasons, deprecation windows for legacy variants, and per-customer eval gate requirements. Goal is to give PMs and SEs a deterministic path (scorecard + approvals) to move requests from inbound to onboarded or deferred while minimizing operational and security risk.
acceptance_criteria: A documented scorecard that scores requests across technical readiness, security/compliance risk, customer ARR impact, and runtime cost delta
A standardized per-customer eval gate template (prompt set + metrics) that product owners can use to validate quality before pinning or onboarding
A defined approval chain for high-risk items (security, data residency, export controls) and a checklist for release + deprecation notices
Integration points identified with ENG tickets for kernel/regression work and with DESIGN for UX copy in the Console change log
updates: 2025-03-10 — Ticket created after backlog review with field SEs; initial problem statement and scope agreed in PM sync.

2025-03-11 — Convened intake workshop with Solutions Engineering (Nadia Ramos), Security (Jordan Liu), and Runtime leads (Priya Das). Collected 12 recent customer requests: 4 new models, 5 version pins, 3 deprecations.
2025-03-12 — Draft scorecard metrics proposed: Technical Maturity (0-5), Regulatory Risk (0-5), ARR Impact (0-5), Performance Cost Delta (0-5). Threshold >=12 recommended to fast-track onboarding.
2025-03-13 — Security flagged two items requiring KMS/HSM integration and data residency review; marked as high-risk and added dependency on ENG-4290 (KMS workstream).
2025-03-14 — Evals lead (Marta Kim) suggested adding hallucination-rate <=2% and factuality precision on domain prompts as gating metrics for generative models. Added to eval template.

2025-03-15 — Trade-off session with Runtime: aggressive quantized variant onboarding could reduce cost but increases support surface; decided to require a staging window with telemetry for 14 days before public catalog listing.
2025-03-17 — Draft playbook reviewed by Legal; export-control clause inserted for certain models. Next: publish internal playbook and pilot with two customer requests (Sales IDs: CUST-221, CUST-304).
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use a numeric scorecard to make intake deterministic; threshold set at 12/20 for expedited pipeline.
Decision: All enterprise pins require tenant-scoped evals and an explicit rollback plan in case of quality regressions.
Trade-off: Allowing experimental quantized builds into dedicated pools improves cost but will require dedicated support label and a 90-day deprecation window for breaking internal KV cache changes.
Security decision: Any model that touches customer-provided PII or requires customer-side fine-tuning must pass KMS and audit-log integration before catalog listing.
next_steps: Publish internal intake form and scorecard (owner: Asha) by 2025-03-20
Create ENG tickets to implement a per-customer staging flag in the catalog API (owner: Liam, see ENG-4142)
Pilot the process with two live customer requests and collect telemetry for the 14-day staging window
Schedule a cross-functional retro after pilot to tune thresholds and rollout cadence
